brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.requirement: A tool rack (a panel that holds tools)
requirements.evidence: Three full bases in one row (piece:-1,0,0;full, piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full) form one joined body (single group in check_build, joint bolts lockJoints, meshClash clear).

requirements.requirement: Hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers
requirements.evidence: Two hex-acc-keyhole accessories (accessory:0#-1,0#1 and accessory:0#1,0#1) on the left and right cells spread the load across the row for screws already in the wall.
Three hex-acc-hook plates (accessory:0#-1,0#2, accessory:0#0,0#1, accessory:0#1,0#2), each carrying two hooks, giving six hooks across the front faces.

finish.summary: Built a 3-hex wide wall tool rack: three full bases joined and bolted in one row, keyhole hangers (hex-acc-keyhole) on the left and right cells for screws already in the wall, and three hook plates (hex-acc-hook, two hooks each = six hooks) across the fronts for small hand tools. Open faces capped and joints locked per house rules. check_build is clean (meshClash clear, no issues). No props were kept: staged tools do not hang on hook plates in the configurator and bench-staged props hung through the bench at ground level, so the hooks are left empty and clearly visible for use.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
